text:
sam: hey all :wave: I accepted the GitHub org invite but I can't see private repos (infra, runtime). Clicking repo links just shows 'Not Found'. Anyone know what I'm missing? My GH handle: sam-lee

maria: welcome @sam! usually that means 2FA or SSO hasn't been completed. Did you enable two-factor auth on your GitHub account?

sam: I set up SMS 2FA yesterday. Could that cause it?

jun: SMS 2FA won't cut it — our org requires TOTP or a hardware key. Go to GitHub Settings -> Security -> "Two-factor authentication" and enable TOTP (Authy/Google) or add a YubiKey. After that you may need to re-accept the invite or grant SSO.

sam: switching to Authy now, brb

kevin: also remember we use SAML SSO for the org. After enabling TOTP, go to https://github.com/orgs/redwood-inference and click the "Grant access" / "Enable SSO" button if prompted. If you still get 404/403, ping me and I'll check the invite.

sam: ok did TOTP. Org page loads but private repos still return 403. Invite status shows "Member (pending SAML)" on the org page.

infra-bot: Invitation status updated for sam-lee: pending_saml -> action_required

lisa: @kevin fyi People Ops may have only done org membership. They still need to be added to team(s) for repo access.

maria: thanks @lisa — I'll add sam to the eng team now. sam, can you confirm your GH username again?

sam: sam-lee (same as above)

maria: added you to the eng team. You should get a GitHub notification. If you don't, check GitHub Settings -> Organizations -> Redwood Inference -> Grant access.

sam: I got the notification and can now open private repos. Huge thanks! Quick follow-up: how do I request write access to redwood-runtime?

jun: for write access, either open a ticket in #eng-infra with repo + GH handle or use the access form (https://internal.redwood.com/it/access-requests). Usually new hires get read; we grant write when onboarding says you're working on that repo. You can also ping @kevin directly.

sam: filed a ticket in #eng-infra with the details. Thanks everyone :tada: 

kevin: looked and added sam-lee as a collaborator to redwood-runtime with write perms. You should see the permission change in a few minutes. If not, react here and I'll troubleshoot.

sam: confirmed, I can push to the repo now. Appreciate it!
